items.title: Kerala High Court refuses interim bail to Reporter TV MD Anto Augustine
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Friday refused to grant interim bail to managing director of Malayalam news channel Reporter TV, Anto Augustine, who sought bail after he was arrested on allegations of possessing liquor in excess of the legally permissible levels under the Kerala Abkari Act. [Anto Augustine v State of Kerala] Justice Kauser Edappagath declined urgent relief after the prosecution informed the court that it has moved an application seeking police custody of Augustine and that he is scheduled to be produced before the magistrate court on Saturday. In view of the custody application, the Court declined to grant interim bail at this stage. However, the Court enquired whether Augustine could be connected to the property from which the alleged liquor was recovered, particularly in view of claim that the property had been sold in SARFESI proceedings in 2022. The judge then asked the prosecution to produce material if available to establish that Augustine was actually in position of the property. The matter will be heard next on September 22. items.title: Delhi High Court allows GST search of advocate's office, says privilege can't bar probe into lawyer's conduct
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Thursday dismissed a plea filed by an advocate challenging a GST Department search at his office and the seizure of his computer and other documents [Puneet Batra v. Union of India & Ors] . A Division Bench of Justices Anil Kshetarpal and Shail Jain ruled that advocate-client privilege cannot operate as an absolute bar against an investigation into the conduct of an advocate. “There can be no dispute that communications and material protected by advocate-client privilege are entitled to the protection recognised in law. However, such privilege cannot operate as an absolute bar against an investigation into the conduct of the Advocate himself, where the Respondents have placed prima facie material indicating that the Petitioner may have acted beyond the role of a legal adviser and may have been involved in the affairs under investigation," the Court observed. items.title: Delhi court grants bail to US national Matthew Aaron VanDyke in Myanmar terror training case
items.summary: A Delhi court on Friday granted default bail to Matthew Aaron Van Dyke, a US national who was arrested by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) in March this year. Special NIA Judge Prashant Sharma of the Rouse Avenue Court granted bail to Van Dyke on a personal bond of ₹1 lakh and a surety of the same amount. In its order, the Court noted that the chargesheet filed by the NIA was "piecemeal" as it pertained to Section 21 and 23 of the Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025 only. It said that as the NIA is still investigating the offences under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA), it cannot be concluded that Van Dyke is not entitled to default bail. "As such, investigating agency cannot circumvent sec. 187(3) BNSS (erstwhile sec. 167(2) CrPC) by filing incomplete charge-sheet, for the purpose of denying default bail to applicant/ accused Matthew Aaron Van Dyke," the Court said. The Court said that while on bail, Van Dyke must stay in Delhi and appear before the NIA whenever required. items.title: NCLT sends Bira, creditors to mediation in insolvency case
items.summary: The National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) at New Delhi has sent Bira and its creditors to mediation to explore a settlement of insolvency proceedings pending against the company. A special bench comprising Judicial Member Ashok Kumar Bhardwaj and Technical Member Ravindra Chaturvedi passed the order on September 15 while hearing multiple proceedings against B9 Beverages Limited, including a Section 7 insolvency plea filed by Unity Small Finance Bank Limited. " It is made clear that if no settlement is arrived between the parties in the meeting directed to be scheduled, no further indulgence would be shown in the matter ," the Tribunal said. The direction came after the Tribunal was told that financiers were willing to infuse funds into the company and revive it. Counsel appearing for the company submitted that settlement discussions were being held with the creditors. However, several creditors expressed reservations about the proposal. Unity Small Finance Bank placed before the Tribunal a September 10 letter to show that an offer of ₹3 crore had been made against dues of over ₹19.04 crore. It argued that the proposal could not be regarded as a serious or plausible settlement offer.

items.title: Ex-DGP Tomin Thachankary moves Kerala High Court challenging conviction in disproportionate assets case
items.summary: Former Kerala Director General of Police (DGP) Tomin J Thachankary has moved the Kerala High Court challenging a Vigilance Court ruling that convicted him in a disproportionate assets case. Kottayam Enquiry Commissioner and Special Judge (Vigilance) KV Rajaneesh had on Thursday passed the verdict after finding that there was a disproportionate income of over ₹30 lakh, which comes up to over 50% of his known income at the time. The trial court proceeed to sentence Thachankary to four years of rigorous imprisonment. While Thachankary had requested for a lighter sentence citing medical ailments, the Court opined that his position did not warrant leniency especially considering the magnitude of his abuse of power. The court also imposed a fine of ₹30.84 lakhs on Thachankary, the exact amount of disproportionate assets it found. Thachankary has now challenged this verdict before the Kerala High Court. The case originated from a complaint filed by Bobby Kuruvila, who claimed to be an anti-corruption crusader. He alleged that Thachankary had acquired houses, flats and other properties during his service disproportionate to his known income. A vigilance investigation launched subsequently

The oral observations by Justice BV Nagarathna and Justice Augustine George Masih came during a hearing on the establishment of Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalayas (JNVs) in Tamil Nadu. The court also gave the state three more months to identify land in every district for setting up the schools, while asking the Union and Tamil Nadu state to resolve their differences through discussions. The dispute, however, goes beyond the question of Hindi. At its core are Tamil Nadu’s two-language policy, the role of the Union in education and whether a state can refuse to implement a centrally funded education scheme on the grounds that it conflicts with its own laws and policies. items.title: Where are the soft skills? Supreme Court advises young lawyers to train under seniors on court decorum
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Friday expressed concern over the declining emphasis on traditional court training and decorum among young lawyers [ Puja Entertainment India Ltd v. TIPS Industries Ltd & Ors. ]. A Bench of Justices BV Nagarathna and AG Masih emphasized that soft skills and advocacy are best learned under the guidance of senior members of the Bar. "Today we are told some youngsters are starting their own office without training. That is really not good. Unless you train with a senior you won’t know the real skills of advocacy, the real tricks of the trade, you will just be wondering. We know youngsters are ambitious. But unless you train with a senior, you won’t know the niceties of the profession. Nowadays, youngsters are so ambitious, but where are the soft skills? Every day from a senior you have to learn. We are concerned about the future of the Bar," it said. items.title: J&K High Court establishes Delhi office for coordination with Supreme Court, Central government
items.summary: The High Court of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh on Friday sanctioned a resident office at New Delhi for better coordination and communication with the Supreme Court and the Union government at the national level. The office will function under the supervision and control of an officer designated as Registrar (Headquarters), New Delhi and report to the Chief Justice through the Registrar General. In an order issued on Friday, Chairman of the J&K Sales Tax Appellate Tribunal Amit Kumar Gupta was asked to function as Registrar (Headquarters), New Delhi till further orders. As per the High Court, the resident office has been established for following purposes: 1.
